subject: SE / Var for model estimate of HR

messages.author: 6156965d24ba19ac
messages.subject: SE / Var for model estimate of HR
parts:
Hi,

I would like to use a meta analysis to investigate the variation in home range estimates across individuals. The metafor package requires either the variance or standard error but the models provide confidence intervals. Do you know how I can either:

1) use the model output (if possible) to calculate SE / Var 
2) calculate SE from the CI

Best,
Jared

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: SE / Var for model estimate of HR
parts:
Hi Jared,

You can extract the parameter estimate covariance matrix from the fit object like FIT$COV. The rows/columns should all have appropriate names.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: SE / Var for model estimate of HR
parts:
Hi Rachel,

I'll put exposing that on the TODO list, but for the moment you could divide the CI width by a z-score CI width (2*1.96 @ 95%) to get an approximate standard error.

This won't account for the correlations between overlaps if you have a bunch of individuals in the same area. That's a whole 'nother paper.

Best,
Chris

messages.author: 40fd627580dd34f5
messages.subject: Re: SE / Var for model estimate of HR
parts:
Hi Rachel,

This is what you would want for the variance and standard error of the area (2D chi^2 relation):

S <- summary(UD)
AREA <- S$CI[1,2]
VAR <- AREA^2 / S$DOF['area']
SE <- sqrt(VAR)

And I would recommend something like a log-link, if possible, in which case you would actually want

log.AREA <- log(AREA)
VAR.log <- 1/ S$DOF['area']
SE.log <- sqrt(VAR.log)

Best,
Chris
